column1: # FLAKE REGISTRY — order/determinism flakes (host-INDEPENDENT), one row per known
# non-deterministic test. Companion to testdata/heavy-tests.tsv; gated in BOTH
# directions by TestFlakeRegistryMatchesTheTestsItNames (internal/standards).
# THIS IS NOT A SUPPRESSION LIST. A suppression entry says "this test may fail";
# a registry row says WHY it fails — the DETERMINISTIC mechanism that makes the
# same code on the same host pass and fail across repetitions, and which ledger
# row fixed or owes the fix. The gate rejects a row whose root_cause column does
# not open with `deterministic: `, because a registry that cannot be told from a
# list of excuses is worse than no registry: it launders a defect into a
# documented condition.
# WHY A FLAKE IS NOT A HEAVINESS CLASS: a heavy test's verdict is the HOST's
# (ambient load, wall clock, sudo) and skipping it on the smoke path is correct —
# there is nothing in the code to fix. A flake is wrong under EVERY host state,
# so routing it through heavytest.Require / CriterionHostCondition would HIDE it
# behind a skip that reads as a passing green. The instrument for this class is
# REPETITION: `go test -count=N` on the test itself (GOPI.md Rule 27 — measure
# the test, never the host; no device load, no pressure generator, ever).
# CATCH: scripts/flake-catch.sh — a named opt-in (`make flake-catch`), OFF the
# smoke/merge path, that re-runs a scope N times and NAMES the tests whose
# verdict moves across repetitions:
#     make flake-catch PKGS='./internal/tools/'
#     make flake-catch PKGS='-reps 20 ./cmd/agent/'
# Columns (TAB-separated):
#   test         the Go test function name (must exist, in `package`)
#   package      the module-relative package directory carrying that test
#   root_cause   `deterministic: <the mechanism>` — one line, DETERMINISTIC
#   owner        the ledger row id that fixed or owes the fix (the FULL id, or
#                the `t-<epoch>` legacy id — never an 8-hex chip, which names
#                more than one row). Never empty: an unowned flake is
#                a flake nobody re-reads (GOPI.md Rule 26 — dispatch again,
#                don't wait). The gate resolves it against the task ledger.
#   date         YYYY-MM-DD the root cause was pinned
# NOTE: the `package` column must be the DIRECTORY ('cmd/agent' — a path, so it
# ends in neither `_test.go` nor `.go`), while the root_cause column QUOTES the
# source file and the exact statements that carried the mechanism, so the next
# reader can go straight to the line instead of re-deriving the diagnosis. The
# two are deliberately different: the column is machine-matched against the test,
# the prose is for the human.
# test
TestTaskFindSessionJSONLStillHonoursEveryLayout
column3: deterministic: the old fixture wrote all three session-record layouts into ONE shared t.TempDir() root and walked them from a Go map (randomized iteration order); the three layouts are alternative ADDRESSES for one session, so whichever address the resolver legitimately prefers, the other two must fail — the verdict is a coin flip on the map's iteration order. FIXED: 14b4ee41 gave each layout its own fixture root and the test now guards the fixture (assertOnlyThisLayoutIsPresent).

column1: TestWorkerBusyRoundResetsIdleStreak
column3: deterministic: the fixture seeded the task row from a goroutine that slept a wall-clock 1.5s and assumed the worker's round would claim the row inside that window; whether the claim and the busy round landed inside the sleep decided the verdict (measured 3/10 FAIL on clean master). FIXED: the seed now runs on the worker loop's idle-drain hook the instant round 1's verdict banks (armWorkerIdleDrainHook) — no wall-clock guess.

column1: TestMemorySearchNonBlocking
column3: deterministic: four concurrent MemoryStore calls race the FIRST-OPEN schema build of a fresh ledger. The winner's initKnowledgeBase is a SEQUENCE of write transactions (ensureSchema's atomic batch, then ensureFeedbackSchema, then ensureTasksSchema), and on a block-backed ledger each commit is a device sync: MEASURED on this host n=121, median 131ms / p90 185ms / max 837ms (internal/tools/firstopen_probe_test.go), i.e. the build legitimately outlasts the losers' bounded poll (waitForDistilledSchema, memory.go:1139 — dbSchemaWaitTries x dbSchemaWaitInterval = 20x25ms = 500ms). Once the budget was spent the loser fell through to the refusal at memory.go:1324 (store) / :1189 (search) / tasks.go:1138 and reported "not a distilled knowledge base (missing distilled_qa table)" for a DB that was merely not built yet — a wall-clock GUESS about another process's progress used as a gate. FIXED (commit 8bb18ecc): the recovery is a fact about the FILE, not a guess — adoptUninitializedKnowledgeBase (memory.go:1207) reads sqlite_master through hasNoSchemaObjects (memory.go:1169) and, when the opened file carries ZERO schema objects, JOINS the initialization under the existing per-path lock instead of refusing; a populated foreign DB (hermes' distilled_knowledge.db, state.db) keeps the refusal byte-for-byte unmutated, because a used file never reads zero objects. Regression guard: TestEmptyFileStoreIsInitializedNotRefused + TestConcurrentFirstOpenWaiterIsNotRefused (internal/tools/firstopen_refusal_regression_test.go), red on the pre-fix tip with this exact message, green after; 20/20 clean under `go test -count=20 -run '^TestMemorySearchNonBlocking$' ./internal/tools/`.

column1: TestTaskRunSurvivesClosedStdoutPipe
column3: deterministic: the wrapper's signal.Ignore(syscall.SIGPIPE) sat BELOW TaskStart (the very call the test waits for before slamming the stdout pipe's read end), so the wrapper's next claim/briefing write to stdout raced the ignore and the default disposition killed it. FIXED: signal.Ignore(syscall.SIGPIPE) hoisted to the top of runTaskRunOnce, before any claim/start/print; evidence in devdoc/sigpipe-flake-fix.md.

column1: TestChatEditingLine_SurvivesALargeToolOutputAtSmallHeights
column3: deterministic: the test synchronized on a DRAIN-counter that is not causally ordered with its own assertion — waitDraws(t, Answer().StatusPublishes()+1) (cmd/agent/chat_stream_test.go) returned as soon as the editor's read loop had serviced the publish's WAKE, while the five scripted keystrokes the same channel had already queued were still unread, so the assertion below read a half-produced screen. MEASURED on the pre-fix tip 2fdc65e4 with the loop parked at the wait (instrumented t.Logf): the wait trips with read=2/5 ("you> he"), read=4/5 ("you> hell") and with the status row still "iter 0" — 2/20 one-shot runs FAIL and -count=100 in ONE process FAILs twice, the same three shapes. FIXED (commit 65d7e278, merged as c74ca08f): the wait is on the ASSERTION'S OWN SUBJECT (the editing row carries the typed text AND the status row carries the published counters, cmd/agent/lineedit_height_test.go), and the invariant moved into a DETERMINISTIC guard, TestChatPublishDoesNotOvertakeQueuedInput, which parks the read loop on a gate, raises a publish, queues keys, then reads the ORDER off the write stream — red 6/6 on rows=4 with the ordering gate neutralized, green with it. Residual, dispatched separately: that guard's harness cannot report a pending backlog (scriptSource does not implement lineedit's inputBacklog; internal/lineedit's scriptedSource could not park its loop), so the guard guards the editor's ORDER decision, not its backlog answer.

column1: TestScratchGCDepsOriginReadsExeNotArgv0
column3: deterministic: the fixture planted `exec.Command(sleepBin,"30")` and then overwrote cmd.Args with ONE field (the Chromium-shaped lie), so the kernel delivered that string as argv[0] and NOTHING as argv[1]: `sleep` had no duration to parse, printed its usage and exited within ~50 µs — MEASURED with a spawn probe (400 spawns per cell): read at 0 delay 0/400 failed, at 50 µs 397/400 failed, at 2 ms and 50 ms 400/400 failed, every failure state=Z (exited, unreaped) — so /proc/<pid>/exe was ENOENT and depsResidentOrigin answered `unknown` where the test demanded `foreign`. Whether the readlink ran inside that sub-50-µs window was the host's business: 21/300 runs red at load ~8. FIXED (this row): the plant carries a real argv[1] duration, and its measurability is ASSERTED as preconditions — argv arity + a duration the program accepts + Signal(0) liveness AND a NON-zombie state read from /proc/<pid>/stat + /proc/<pid>/exe reading back the started executable, before and after the classifier's read — so an unmeasurable plant fails loudly instead of measuring `unknown` (the assertion itself is unchanged, and a revert of depsResidentOrigin to the argv[0] rule still turns the case red with `gopi`).

column1: # RETIRED ROW (2026-09-19, epic merger-delete-dead-impl): the row above for
# TestMergerTakeoverRefusedProbeLeavesTheFDAlive was removed with the test it
# named. The SUBJECT went too — cmd/agent/merger_takeover_lock.go deleted
# detachInheritedFDWrapper and the borrowed-fd adoption path
# (mergerTakeoverLockAdopt), so the wrapper no longer exists and its guard has
# nothing to run against.
# CARRIED FORWARD, because the mechanism is NOT merger-specific: os.NewFile
# installs runtime.SetFinalizer(f, (*file).close), so an *os.File wrapper around
# a descriptor THIS PROCESS DID NOT OPEN will be closed by the finalizer and the
# kernel then RECYCLES that number onto an unrelated live handle (measured: fd 7
# = a TempDir recursion directory; strace showed the close from
# runtime.runfinq). SEVEN os.NewFile sites survive this deletion —
# cmd/agent/cli_worker_daemon.go:564,699; cmd/agent/cli_daemon_spawn.go:627,667;
# internal/daemonlifetime/daemonlifetime.go:169;
# internal/testutil/lifetimeprobe.go:122 — and ANY of them can hit it if the
# wrapper is dropped instead of retained or detached (runtime.SetFinalizer(f,
# nil)). Filed as a Rule-26 dispatch rather than fixed here: it is outside this
# epic's scope (this branch deletes code; it does not rework the spawn path).
TestProbeMeasuresDepthFromRealAnswers
column3: deterministic: the pty responder wrote one reply per query while ranging a Go MAP (randomized order), so the probe's reads returned an arbitrary SUBSET of the answer set; the stop predicate was itself a SUBSET test (CursorPositionReport && (Colors>0 || RGBKnown)), which is satisfiable with replies still in flight, so the probe exited EARLY on a partial stream and reported colors=0 for a terminal that had answered 256. MEASURED on the pre-fix tip (100 reps, both sides instrumented): 31 FAIL, EVERY failing dump elapsed_ms=0 (an early exit, never a window expiry), responder at wrote=2..5 of 5 replies, captured bytes short of the answer set's 84 (32/57/59/60/67) — no clock involved, so a longer window or a settle delay could not have fixed it. FIXED (this branch): probeAnswersComplete now names EVERY question the probe asked, and the fixture declares its answer order in a LIST with the depth replies FIRST and holds each reply until TIOCINQ on the reader's own descriptor reports the previous one read. Guard: TestProbeReadsEveryDepthAnswerOneReadBoundaryAtATime, red 20/20 on the pre-fix predicate with byte-short captures (35/52/59 of 84) and green after.

column1: TestTaskStatusSelectorAndRowIDPrintTheSameVerdict
column3: deterministic: the fixture's row records a runner identity, so `gopi task status` prints a clock-derived start instant on BOTH addresses, computed at RENDER time as boot = now - /proc/uptime (procStartTimeDisplay, internal/tools/taskproc.go:900). /proc/uptime is read with CENTISECOND precision, so that computed boot carries a sawtooth of up to 10 ms that depends only on WHEN the renderer reads the file: a start instant lying inside that sawtooth of a wall-clock second boundary renders :NN for one invocation and :NN+1 for the next. MEASURED on this host by driving the real renderer (taskProcessStatus + TaskProcessStatusReport) over the tick phase: at tick offsets whose instant sits on the boundary the ONE row rendered 'start=2026-10-09T08:19:27+08:00' and 'start=2026-10-09T08:19:28+08:00' across 24 renders (1 of 100 phase positions risky, ~10 ms window), while 400 real CLI invocations of the seeded row in one process all read one value (200 pairs, 0 raw mismatches) — so the failure needs the fixture's instant to sit in that window, i.e. ~10 ms in 1 s per invocation, not the 1 s the two sequential invocations take. FIXED: the two addresses' renders are compared through statusVerdictDiff, which normalises exactly the clock-derived shapes (RFC3339 instants + the 'started_at:' column) and compares every other byte raw; TestTaskStatusVerdictComparisonCatchesAGenuinelyDifferentVerdict drives that same comparison red for a changed verdict word / row address / resumable flag and green for a clock-only difference.

column1: TestStartedDaemonIsReapedSoItsParentLeavesNoZombie
column3: deterministic: THE ARM'S OWN VERDICT RACED THE COLLECT WINDOW, and its own first poll is at t=0. A child that exits is state=Z from the instant the kernel releases it until its parent's Wait reaches it — that interval is what wait(2) semantics ARE, so no seam can remove it. The arm failed on the FIRST reading of Z, i.e. anywhere inside that window. MEASURED through the real seam (workerDaemonSpawnErr, systemd-scope mode) with a 200-microsecond passive sampler, 5 arms: the Z entry was first readable at +1.156/+1.193/+1.198/+1.156/+1.214 ms after SIGKILL and /proc released at +2.048/+2.294/+2.146/+2.323/+2.86 ms — a transient of 0.9..1.2 ms, while the entry was otherwise state=S. The rate follows the poll's phase against that window: MEASURED on the pre-fix tree, 2 FAIL of 120 runs in ONE process (`go test -count=120 -run TestStartedDaemonIsReapedSoItsParentLeavesNoZombie ./cmd/agent/`), each at 0.09s / 0.13s elapsed with the error text carrying the FIRST-poll Z, against 0 FAIL of 118 archived multi-package streams — the archive under-sampled a rate IN-PROCESS repetition reaches. The arm also ATTRIBUTED that Z to os.Getpid() without ever reading stat's ppid field, which Rule 24 forbids. FIXED (this row): a Z reading is now a failure only when it PERSISTS past drzZombieCollectGrace (2s, ~700-1700x the largest measured transient), and the message carries the parent read from /proc/<pid>/stat rather than assumed. Nothing else changed: the same seam, the same SIGKILL-by-explicit-pid, the same assertions. RED-then-GREEN is measured, not asserted — with daemonReapStartedChild disabled (pre-fix behaviour) the guard FAILS 3/3 naming `has been a ZOMBIE (state="Z") for 2.01s`, and 0/120 with it.

column1: TestSignalRecordSenderCommSurvivesAnExitedSender
column3: deterministic: THE ARM ASSERTED A SCHEDULING OUTCOME, NOT PRODUCT BEHAVIOUR. It demanded r.SenderComm == "" for a sender that "exited", but the product records /proc/<sender_pid>/comm AT SIGNAL TIME (signalrec.go:538 field comment; the single write site is stampSignalSource at signalrec.go:2155, `if comm := procString(int(pid), commFileName); comm != ""`), so it writes whatever that read answers. sender.Wait() only reaps the `kill` child when this test process is scheduled to it, and the comm read happens in the VICTIM when the signal is delivered — so on the runs where the handler read /proc before the zombie was collected the field carried the child own comm ("kill", still readable on a zombie) and the arm went red; on the runs where the collect won the race the field was empty and the arm passed. Both records are correct, which makes the red a measurement of scheduler order: 5 of 30 repetitions before the fix.
